main_body: A flat sand ground patch (4x3 tiles) with sparse speckles and a small pink flower; a terrain tile with no standing volume.
top_band: none (flat ground texture; column scan shows only speckle variation between #e2c584 and #f1dca2, no top/front structure)
evidence: The kind is terrain, a ground patch rather than a standing object. The 3/4 contract does not apply, and the drawing is a uniform sand surface with scattered speckles. It has no top or front structure, so it is not a front elevation or any other failing drawing. Part A passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 3 colours per tile, against 26 for the grass reference and 80 distinct colours. The sand is mostly one flat tone (#e2c584) with sparse lighter and darker single-pixel speckles and a single pink flower cluster. There are only about 3 lightness steps, with no grain clumps, pebbles or per-area shading. The sand is much shallower than the grass reference, and the paving reference, though it has only 7 colours, carries stone-by-stone shading and structure. 10% flat-fill coverage against 0% for both references confirms large flat areas. A careful artist would find it thinner and flatter than the reference.
